fixture: synthetic test data for an invented issuer, not issuer evidence
evidence_class: screening_run
Screen the financial change, credit, liquidity, market and legal position of Harbourline Synthetic Foods plc as of 2025-03-31 and name where a full assessment is needed.

The invented issuer looks adequate on liquidity and weaker on earnings, refinancing and document protection, so a full assessment is needed.
Basis: harbourline_annual_report.txt, page 12

Earnings and margins weakened, leverage rose slightly and the main bond falls due in a tight lending period.
Basis: harbourline_annual_report.txt, page 20

sections.heading: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

blocks.text:
Strong cash and an undrawn facility argue against a weaker view; a failed refinancing or a lost facility would worsen it.
Basis: harbourline_annual_report.txt, page 34
- Invented data only, so no conclusion carries weight.

cells: The annual report and one interim statement cover the same perimeter.
Confirm the perimeter in the next report
Operating margin fell by about one point on input costs.
Cash conversion held broadly steady against the prior year.
Leverage rose slightly while interest cover stayed adequate.
Cash and an undrawn facility cover the next two years of maturities.
One reported measure changed definition between years.
Ask the issuer for restated figures
Demand is stable and the customer base is broad.
Margin and free cash flow resilience
Free cash flow stays positive under a modest cost shock.
Refinancing falls in a period of tighter lending.
The owner has paid small dividends and no large distributions.
Stated policy favours debt reduction over acquisitions.
Transition cost is disclosed in general terms only.
Accessible cash exceeds planned uses over the next year.
Working capital, capex and cash burn
Working capital swings are seasonal and capex is flexible.
Most debt is fixed and a small floating part is hedged.
Input costs are partly passed on to customers.
A downside case reduces cover but does not breach the covenant.
The tightest point is the refinancing of the main bond.
Prices are dated and taken from one dealer quote.
The senior bond trades wide of two close comparables.
Issue size is small and trading is thin.
The senior bond ranks ahead of the junior notes.
Documents allow some debt to move ahead of this bond.
Compensation looks fair for the risks found so far.
The bond terms are available but the credit agreement is not.
Two protections look weak in the bond terms.
Guarantees cover most but not all operating entities.
Terms permit some value to leave the group.
The remaining debt capacity is limited by the leverage test.
Recompute capacity in the full assessment
Document gaps are the first priority for the full assessment.
